statement: For every language recognized by an LRNN over exact rational arithmetic under the assumptions of Claim 1, there is a polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean NC circuit family of depth O(log n log* n). Relative to a TC0/transformer simulation in O(log n) bounded-fan-in depth, the asymptotic multiplicative overhead is O(log* n).

existential: a polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean circuit family
quantifiers.obligation: The Boolean family recognizes exactly the same language with depth O(log n log* n).

assumptions: The Claim 1 FO-uniform PNC1 arithmetic circuit construction is available.
Rational gates are represented by integer numerator-denominator pairs with nonzero denominators.
Jung's depth-efficient arithmetic-to-Boolean simulation applies to the resulting polynomial-size integer circuit family.
The transformer comparator is only the standard TC0 subset NC1 upper bound; this is not an architecture-specific wall-clock claim.

anchors: appendix-arithQ.tex:12-35 (Q gate lift and Boolean simulation)

primary_reference.title: Depth efficient transformations of arithmetic into boolean circuits
primary_reference.author: Hermann Jung

pass_condition: The derivation certificate composes the Claim 1 arithmetic depth, a correct constant-depth Q-to-Z gate lift, and Jung's O(d(n) log* n) simulation; symbolic expansion is dominated by O(log n log* n); exact rational operations agree with an independent checker; and the printed bc-denominator control is rejected.
fail_condition: Any source or DOI mismatch, missing derivation step, symbolic depth mismatch, rational-operation mismatch, or negative-control pass exits nonzero.
limitations: The checker independently reconstructs the corollary and validates the rational gate lift and asymptotic substitution. Jung's 1985 arithmetic-to-Boolean simulation is an explicit trusted primary theorem; its Chinese-remainder construction is not re-formalized here. Big-O does not assert the historical verifier's sampled exact depth formula or a hardware latency constant.
